title: Flat-test comparison and tensor pairing for quasi-coherent module pushforward
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\mathcal X,\mathcal Y$ be algebraic stacks over $S$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. Use their big fppf sites and structure sheaves from [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra], module sheaves from [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and quasi-coherent modules meaning modules locally presented by small sums of the structure sheaf. Let $f:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism], and use the module right adjoint $R_f$ and comparison $i_{f,F}$ of [lem-sfb-stack-qcqs-module-adjunction]. A scheme test $t:T\to\mathcal Y$ is flat when its scheme charts are flat [def-weil-flat-morphism]. If $t$ is flat, the map $$i_{f,F}(t):(R_fF)(t)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}T,F|_{\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}T})$$ is an isomorphism for every quasi-coherent module $F$. These comparisons are natural in $F$ and in arrows between flat tests. Use sheaf tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. For quasi-coherent modules $F,G$ the canonical pairing $R_fF\otimes R_fG\to R_f(F\otimes G)$ is the transpose of $f^*(R_fF\otimes R_fG)\simeq f^*R_fF\otimes f^*R_fG\xrightarrow{\epsilon_F\otimes\epsilon_G}F\otimes G$, where $\epsilon$ is the adjunction counit. Under $i_f$ this pairing is the ordinary section tensor pairing into $f_*(F\otimes G)$. The transpose $\mathcal O_{\mathcal Y}\to R_f\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}$ of $f^*\mathcal O_{\mathcal Y}\simeq\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}$ likewise agrees with pullback of regular functions under $i_f$.

source.place: Tag 0GQQ, lemma-direct-image-quasi-coherent-over-flat, degree zero; Tag 0GQR, remark-direct-image-quasi-coherent-tensor, canonical square with the naive cup product. The unit is the adjoint of the structure-ring map.

proof.text: Put $H=f_*F$. By [lem-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-scheme-restriction], the quasi-coherent $F$ is locally quasi-coherent and has all scheme-arrow tensor comparisons invertible, hence has flat comparison maps. Apply [lem-sfb-stack-higher-images-flat-comparison] with $i=0$: $H$ belongs to $\mathcal L_{\mathcal Y}$ of [lem-sfb-stack-lqc-coherator], and $H(t)=\Gamma(\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}T,F|_{\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}T})$. Thus the coherator $QH$ and its counit $q_H$ are available.

source.place: Tag 077A, proposition-direct-image-quasi-coherent, proof; Tag 0GQQ, lemma-direct-image-quasi-coherent-over-flat, reduction to the coherator.

proof.text: The adjunction and compatibility statement of [lem-sfb-stack-qcqs-module-adjunction] say that composition with $i=i_{f,F}$ gives bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(G,R_fF)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(G,H)$ for quasi-coherent $G$: compose its transpose bijection with the ordinary module-sheaf bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction]. That ordinary adjunction applies by [lem-sfb-fibred-fppf-ringed-inverse-image]. Composition with $q=q_H$ gives the same bijections for $QH$ by [lem-sfb-stack-lqc-coherator]. Let $a:R_fF\to QH$ and $b:QH\to R_fF$ be the unique maps with $qa=i$ and $ib=q$. Then $q(ab)=q$ and $i(ba)=i$; injectivity of the respective bijections gives $ab=1$ and $ba=1$. Hence $a$ is an isomorphism and $i=qa$. These identities also make $a$ natural in $F$, by the uniqueness in the same bijections.

source.place: Tag 077A, proposition-direct-image-quasi-coherent, displayed Hom bijections: elementary comparison of their representing objects.

proof.text: For flat $t:T\to\mathcal Y$, apply [lem-sfb-stack-coherator-flat-test-restriction] to $H$ from step 1. Its $q_H(t)$ is invertible; so is $a(t)$ from step 2. Therefore $i_{f,F}(t)=q_H(t)a(t)$ is invertible and has the required target. Naturality in $F$ and in arrows of flat tests is the restriction of the natural module-sheaf map $i$ in [lem-sfb-stack-qcqs-module-adjunction]; no flatness of the arrow between the tests is required.

source.place: Tag 0GQQ, lemma-direct-image-quasi-coherent-over-flat, degree zero, using the coherator restriction of Tag 0GQK.

proof.text: The structure module and tensor products of quasi-coherent modules are quasi-coherent by [lem-sfb-stack-qcoh-flat-atlas-exactness]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor] to the ringed-topos map of [lem-sfb-fibred-fppf-ringed-inverse-image], using the fixed small-site universes. It gives the natural isomorphism $\phi:f^*(R_fF\otimes R_fG)\simeq f^*R_fF\otimes f^*R_fG$. Under the adjunction of [lem-sfb-stack-qcqs-module-adjunction], define $\mu$ to be the transpose of $(\epsilon_F\otimes\epsilon_G)\phi$. This defines the stated canonical pairing and is functorial because all its defining maps and the transpose bijections are natural.

source.place: Tag 0GQR, remark-direct-image-quasi-coherent-tensor, canonical pairing; sites-modules.tex Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, for the tensor comparison.

proof.text: Write $c:f_*F\otimes f_*G\to f_*(F\otimes G)$ for the sheaf map induced by the bilinear section map $(s,t)\mapsto s\otimes t$ on each fibre product. The tensor definition [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] extends this map from presheaf tensors by sheafification. By [lem-sfb-stack-qcqs-module-adjunction], $i_{f,F\otimes G}\mu$ is the ordinary adjunct of $(\epsilon_F\otimes\epsilon_G)\phi$, and $i_{f,F}$ is the ordinary adjunct of $\epsilon_F$ (take $h=1$), likewise for $G$. At an object $x$ of $\mathcal X$, the adjunct counit evaluates a section on the fibre product at its tautological object $x$. Consequently both the transpose of $c(i_{f,F}\otimes i_{f,G})$ and $(\epsilon_F\otimes\epsilon_G)\phi$ send the pure tensor pulled back from $s,t$ to $\epsilon_F(s)\otimes\epsilon_G(t)$. Pullback is precomposition with unchanged structure ring by [lem-sfb-fibred-fppf-ringed-inverse-image]; hence this is the defining pure-tensor comparison, and the maps agree on presheaf tensors, thus on their sheafifications. Injectivity of the ordinary adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] gives $i_{f,F\otimes G}\mu=c(i_{f,F}\otimes i_{f,G})$. This comparison holds on all tests, without asserting $i$ invertible there.

source.place: Tag 0GQR, remark-direct-image-quasi-coherent-tensor, commutative square: elementary verification on bilinear sections of the adjoint-defined pairing.

proof.text: Let $\nu:\mathcal O_{\mathcal Y}\to R_f\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}$ be the transpose of $f^*\mathcal O_{\mathcal Y}\simeq\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}$, the structure-module identification of [lem-sfb-fibred-fppf-ringed-inverse-image]. By [lem-sfb-stack-qcqs-module-adjunction], $i_{f,\mathcal O}\nu$ is its ordinary module adjunct. For $t:T\to\mathcal Y$ this sends $r\in\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ to the compatible family of its pullbacks on objects of $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}T$: evaluation at each such object is the structure-ring map. This is exactly pullback of regular functions under the structure sheaf and global-section conventions of [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra].

source.place: Tag 0GQR, remark-direct-image-quasi-coherent-tensor, unit analogue; stacks-sheaves.tex Tag 06WE, equation-functoriality-sheaves-modules, structure-ring map.

proof_origin.place: Tags 0GQQ and 0GQR, with the adjunction characterization of Tag 077A and elementary bilinear-section verification of the pairing.
